title: checked, nameof, sizeof
hook: `checked` makes integer overflow throw. `nameof` is a compiler-evaluated string of a symbol. `sizeof` is for unmanaged value types, not objects on the heap.

sections.heading: Overflow, symbol names, sizes
sections.prose: By default, `int` arithmetic wraps in an unchecked context (`int.MaxValue + 1` becomes `MinValue`). `checked { }` or a `checked(...)` expression throws `OverflowException` — use it when a count of concurrent attempts must not silently wrap. Project-wide checked arithmetic is an msbuild property; most BCL code assumes unchecked. `nameof(RetryCount)` is `"RetryCount"` even if you rename via IDE refactor. As of C# 14, `nameof(List<>)` is `"List"` — you no longer invent a dummy `List<int>` just to name the open generic. `nameof` on a parameter is the usual argument-exception message. `sizeof(int)` is `4`; `sizeof` on a custom struct works in `unsafe` or when the type is unmanaged. It is not JavaScript `typeof` and it is not the GC size of an object — that discussion is module 14.

snippets.label: checked overflow vs nameof unbound generic
snippets.explanation: Wrong: concatenating "n" by hand in exception messages. Right: nameof. Wrong: sizeof(string) — string is a reference type.

interviewTakeaways: Default arithmetic is unchecked wraparound unless you opt into checked.
`nameof` is compile-time and rename-safe; C# 14 allows unbound generics like `List<>`.
`sizeof` applies to unmanaged value types, not class instances.
commonPitfalls: Using `typeof(List<>).Name` in older code when `nameof(List<>)` is now legal and clearer.
Assuming `sizeof` equals memory a SkiaSharp bitmap occupies — it does not.
Wrapping a whole service in `checked` and surprising yourself on `GetHashCode` style math.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS numbers are IEEE-754; they do not wrap like int32. `typeof` is runtime. C# `nameof` is compile-time; `sizeof` is a constant for unmanaged types.
